why: p04's full beat thumps in at 0:21 under a wistful, melancholy loop, while p17 just rocks between two chords like a music-box lullaby and only pauses at 0:36.

Both are dark late-night beats, but p18 has the bigger arrival (+10 dB at 0:20 after a swelling pad intro) and breathes more with its drumless breakdown near 2:54, while p05 sits on one loop and has only the short drum cut at 2:55.
p03 opens muffled and then the drums drop in at 0:13 on a moody, slightly uneasy loop, while p17 is a gentle, lullaby-like mallet sketch whose only event is the ringing pause at 0:36.

p05's dark keys give way to a hard drum-and-808 entry at 0:10 and a melancholy late-night groove, while p19 is hypnotic and wistful, with drums coming and going and a lift at 0:54, but it is a bit tense and over too soon to pull you in.
Both are moody beats with filtered intros, but p18's drop at 0:20 hits harder and its drumless C/Ab breakdown near 2:54 breathes more than p03's single thinned-drum stretch at 2:02.

p18 is dark and hypnotic, with a big beat drop at 0:20 and drumless breaks, while p02 is a fun game-style synth rush that opens up at 0:37 but then stays at one pumping level apart from the 1:21 breakdown.

p02 bursts from a muffled intro into full tilt at 0:37 and has a dark breakdown with a singing lead at 1:21, while p20 is a pastel, swaying keys loop whose darker Fm9 peak at 0:56 is brief and fades out fast.
p02 has a real arrival when the filter opens at 0:37 and a darker Phrygian colour, while p16 is a cheerful, bright anime-style cue that stays at one level even through its wistful turn at bar 23.
p03 is a moody late-night beat whose muffled intro opens as the drums drop in at 0:13, while p16 is bright and happy-nostalgic with only a one-bar break at 0:58 to vary it.

p01 is a moody, head-nodding beat with a satisfying dark turn at the end of each cycle (for example around 0:48), while p17 is a soft, pretty music-box rock between Fmaj7 and Cmaj9 that barely changes after its pause at 0:36.
p05's dark, bittersweet loop lands hard when the drums and 808 come in at 0:10, while p20 floats in a pastel, waltz-like sway and only darkens briefly at 0:56.

p19's bittersweet one-note ostinato pulls you in and breathes as the drums drop out at 0:45 before the lift at 0:54, while p02 is energetic but mostly circles one synth pattern at a flat level after its 0:37 opening.

p05 is a dark, melancholy groove that hits when the drums drop at 0:10 and breathes in the 2:55 breakdown, while p17 is a gentle lullaby-style mallet sketch whose only event is letting a chord ring at 0:36.
